hero.headline: Senate Republicans remove $1 billion White House ballroom funding from budget bill
hero.body:
Senate Republicans have stripped language from a revised budget reconciliation bill that would have allocated up to $1 billion for security upgrades to a proposed White House ballroom. The decision was made internally before the Memorial Day recess, with the change becoming public when the revised package was released Wednesday.

The ballroom project, championed by President Trump, would have created a 90,000-square-foot facility on White House grounds. The removal marks a significant setback for the initiative after the funding had been included in earlier versions of the reconciliation package that Republicans are using to advance budget priorities without Democratic support.

Budget reconciliation allows the majority party to pass fiscal legislation with a simple majority in the Senate, bypassing the standard 60-vote threshold required to overcome a filibuster. This procedural tool enables Republicans to advance their budget agenda without needing Democratic votes.

The decision to remove the ballroom provision came after internal discussions among Senate Republicans, who control the chamber. The revised bill was unveiled Wednesday without the ballroom language, representing a significant change from the earlier draft. Senate Republican leadership did not provide a public explanation for the removal or the timing of the announcement.

The reconciliation package continues progressing through the legislative process without the ballroom funding included. The move reflects internal GOP calculations about what provisions could survive the legislative process and maintain party unity on the broader budget package.

This development comes as Congress navigates significant fiscal and policy disagreements. The Senate has been engaged in disputes with House Republican leadership over government funding, particularly regarding Department of Homeland Security appropriations. House Speaker Mike Johnson has indicated his chamber will pursue alternative funding approaches, setting up potential conflicts between the two chambers over budget priorities.

The broader reconciliation effort remains one of the Republican majority's main vehicles for advancing the Trump administration's policy agenda. With Democrats unable to block reconciliation measures that stay within budgetary parameters, Republicans have been working to include various priorities in these bills.

The White House has not yet commented publicly on the removal of the ballroom provision from the reconciliation bill. It remains unclear whether the administration will pursue alternative funding mechanisms for the proposed facility or whether the project will be shelved entirely.

The decision by Senate Republicans to strip the funding suggests concern among some members about the optics of allocating such substantial resources to the project during a period of significant government funding debates and fiscal pressures. The removal allows Republicans to focus the reconciliation bill on other priorities while potentially addressing concerns from members who questioned the appropriateness of the ballroom expenditure.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes Tariffs on 60 Countries Over Forced Labor
cards.teaser: The administration proposed a 10 percent tariff on Canada, Mexico, the European Union and dozens of other trading partners, citing forced labor concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has proposed tariffs between 10 and 12.5 percent on 60 trading partners, including Canada, Mexico, the UK, the EU, Taiwan and Australia. The administration is citing forced labor concerns as the justification for the trade restrictions.

The EU has responded by challenging the proposal, stating it expected the US to honor a tariff agreement reached in July and arguing that the new levies violate the spirit of that deal. The administration appears to be using forced labor allegations as a legal rationale for imposing tariffs, a shift from previous trade policy justifications.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg as Putin Economic Conference Begins
cards.teaser: Ukraine launched strikes targeting a navy base and oil terminal near Russia's second-largest city on the first day of an annual economic conference.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones attacked oil storage facilities near St. Petersburg as President Putin's annual economic forum opened. President Zelensky confirmed the strikes targeted an oil terminal in the region, with reports indicating the facility caught fire.

The timing placed the attack at the start of a major economic event hosted by Putin. The strikes continue Ukraine's campaign against Russian military and energy infrastructure in areas previously considered safer from attack.

cards.headline: Trump nominates housing official Bill Pulte as director of national intelligence
cards.teaser: Senator Mitch McConnell issued a warning about qualifications needed for the intelligence post after the nomination was announced.
cards.body:
President Trump has nominated Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as director of national intelligence. The role requires overseeing 18 intelligence agencies and serving as the president's principal intelligence adviser.

Senator Mitch McConnell issued a statement Wednesday cautioning that anyone appointed to the position must possess "extensive national security experience." Senator Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, has also raised concerns about Pulte's appointment.

cards.headline: Iran Attacks Kuwait Airport, Killing One and Injuring Dozens
cards.body:
A drone strike on Kuwait's international airport killed one person and wounded 63 others, marking the deadliest attack on a Gulf nation since a ceasefire between the United States and Iran took effect on April 8. The assault damaged a passenger terminal and represented a significant escalation in the fragile truce between Washington and Tehran.

Kuwait's military confirmed the Iranian attack targeted the terminal building, causing substantial damage to the structure. The country's civil aviation authority suspended traffic at the airport and redirected incoming flights to alternative locations. Kuwait's defense ministry spokesperson, Brigadier General Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan, called the strike "criminal Iranian aggression which resulted in significant material damage to the building and injuries."

The attack followed a chain of military exchanges in the Gulf region. U.S. forces had fired a Hellfire missile at an Iranian oil tanker, the M/T Lexie, as it attempted to reach Iran's Kharg Island near Kuwait. American Central Command stated that aircraft disabled the tanker's engine after the crew ignored repeated warnings over 24 hours. The tanker was traveling through international waters in the strait of Hormuz.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responded by striking Kuwait's airport and claimed to have attacked the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones. The U.S. military denied the Bahrain claims. American forces also said they shot down three Iranian drones launched toward civilian vessels in regional waters.

In response to the escalation, Kuwait took diplomatic action. The country's deputy foreign minister summoned Iran's charge d'affaires to lodge a formal protest. Kuwait ordered a reduction in Iranian embassy staff, declared two Iranian diplomats persona non grata, and gave them 24 hours to leave.

Iran's foreign ministry blamed Kuwait and Bahrain for the attacks, stating they allowed the United States to use their territory for aggressive operations against Iran. The statement called the incident proof of "the direct and unmistakable responsibility of the leaders of Kuwait and Bahrain for last night's acts of aggression."

Mohsen Rezaee, military adviser to Iran's supreme leader, warned that further American attacks would be met with "a deluge of missiles and drones." He stated that "the aggressor will swiftly be punished."

President Trump said negotiations with Iran were continuing and that he was not seeking to escalate the conflict. He expressed interest in meeting with Iran's supreme leader but made derogatory comments about his health.

The exchange of strikes highlights the fragility of ceasefire efforts despite claims from U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio that the war in Iran "is over" and that a nuclear agreement was within reach. Iran's foreign minister indicated the country would suspend peace talks in protest of Israeli military operations in Lebanon, threatening to derail negotiations with Washington.

cards.headline: Hotel Fire in New Delhi Kills at Least 21
cards.teaser: A fire at a hotel in India's capital killed at least 21 people and injured dozens more.
cards.body:
A fire at a hotel in New Delhi killed at least 21 people, authorities said. Dozens more were injured in the blaze, which appears to be the deadliest fire in the Indian capital in at least four years.

The fire broke out at the hotel, though the cause has not been determined. Emergency responders worked to evacuate guests and extinguish the flames. The death toll makes this one of the most serious fire incidents in New Delhi in recent years.

cards.headline: Trump confirms calling Netanyahu crazy in phone conversation
cards.teaser: President Trump acknowledged he used the word crazy to describe Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a phone call.
cards.body:
President Trump confirmed he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu crazy during a phone conversation. Netanyahu downplayed the clash, saying he and Trump have tactical disagreements but agree on broader issues related to Iran.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed hope that ongoing talks between Lebanon and Israel will end hostilities in the region. The exchange between Trump and Netanyahu comes amid questions about U.S. policy toward operations against Hezbollah. Netanyahu characterized the disagreement as tactical rather than strategic.

cards.body:
Ukrainian drones attacked oil storage facilities near St. Petersburg as President Putin's annual economic forum opened. President Zelensky confirmed the strikes targeted an oil terminal in the region, with reports indicating the facility caught fire.

The timing placed the attack at the start of a major economic event hosted by Putin. The strikes continue Ukraine's campaign against Russian military and energy infrastructure in areas previously considered safer from attack.

cards.headline: Violent Protests Erupt in UK Over Murder Case
cards.teaser: Eleven police officers were injured in protests after politicians and commentators accused authorities of bias in the Henry Nowak murder case.
cards.body:
Demonstrations over the Henry Nowak murder case escalated into violence in the United Kingdom, with 11 police officers injured during clashes with protesters. Right-wing politicians and commentators had accused police of showing anti-white bias in their handling of the case, fueling the demonstrations.

National leaders have called for calm as tensions remain elevated. The protests have drawn significant attention from senior officials, who have urged demonstrators to allow the legal process to proceed without further disruption.

cards.headline: FBI Kills Hostage-Taker at California Bank
cards.teaser: A man who took hostages at a California bank was shot dead by FBI agents after a standoff that lasted two days.
cards.body: An armed man took hostages at a California bank, prompting an FBI response. The situation unfolded over two days, with two hostages released on Tuesday. The remaining hostages were freed on Wednesday, all unharmed. FBI agents ultimately shot and killed the hostage-taker to resolve the standoff.

cards.headline: Four Sentenced to Death for Nigeria Church Massacre
cards.teaser: A court sentenced four men to death for killing worshippers at a Catholic church in Nigeria.
cards.body:
Four men received death sentences for killing worshippers at a Catholic church in Nigeria. A fifth man was discharged and acquitted due to insufficient evidence against him.

The court handed down the sentences following proceedings related to the attack on the church. The massacre of worshippers at the Catholic church had drawn widespread condemnation when it occurred.

cards.headline: Drone Strike Kills Eight on Bus in Russian-Occupied Ukraine
cards.teaser: A drone struck a bus in the eastern Donetsk region, killing eight people.
cards.body:
Eight people were killed when a drone struck a bus in the eastern Donetsk region of Ukraine, which is under Russian control, according to local officials. The bus was traveling through the occupied territory when it was hit.

The attack is part of the broader conflict in Ukraine, where civilian infrastructure continues to face strikes amid the ongoing war.

hero.headline: Trump-backed candidate loses Iowa GOP governor primary to MAHA-aligned farmer
hero.body:
Zach Lahn won the Republican primary for Iowa governor on Tuesday, defeating Randy Feenstra, a congressman who had secured Donald Trump's endorsement. The result marks the first time since March that a Trump-backed candidate has lost a primary election.

Feenstra, who represents Iowa's 4th congressional district, finished in second place despite the former president's support. Lahn emerged victorious in a five-candidate race, positioning himself to face Democrat Rob Sand, the state auditor, in November's general election.

The outcome represents a significant moment for Trump's political influence within Republican primary contests. Until Tuesday's elections, every candidate Trump endorsed since March had won their primary races. The Iowa governor's race broke that pattern.

Lahn's victory comes as the Make America Healthy Again movement has been gaining attention within Republican politics. While the source material does not provide specific details about Lahn's policy positions or MAHA alignment, his win may reflect shifting dynamics among Iowa Republican voters.

Iowa has long served as a bellwether state for national political trends. Democrats view the state as competitive this cycle, believing they have strong candidates in the governor's race and three of the state's four congressional districts. The state has been controlled by Republicans for the past decade, but party strategists see opportunities for Democratic gains.

In the Democratic gubernatorial primary, Rob Sand ran unopposed and secured his party's nomination. Sand is currently the last Democrat holding statewide elected office in Iowa.

The governor's race will be one of several competitive contests across the state heading into November. Iowa voters also participated in primaries for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by Republican Joni Ernst, as well as House races in multiple districts.

The gubernatorial primary results have prompted broader questions about the durability of Trump's endorsement power, particularly as new political movements gain traction within the Republican Party. Observers of national politics are watching whether Trump's influence in primary elections has reached its limits or whether Tuesday's Iowa result represents an isolated incident.

Lahn will campaign against Sand over the coming months. The general election will test whether Iowa voters support the direction signaled by Lahn's primary victory or prefer the Democratic alternative. The race is expected to draw significant attention as one of the competitive gubernatorial contests that could shape the political landscape heading into the 2028 presidential election cycle.

Republicans have held Iowa's governor's mansion since 2011, giving the party a significant advantage in the state's political landscape.

cards.headline: Three Royal Navy personnel killed in helicopter crash during training
cards.teaser: A Royal Navy helicopter crashed during a training exercise in Devon, killing all three people on board.
cards.body:
A Royal Navy helicopter crashed during a training exercise in Devon, resulting in three deaths. The incident occurred during routine training operations with all three people aboard the aircraft killed.

Following the tragedy, the Royal Family, Prime Minister, and head of the Navy issued condolences to those affected by the crash.

cards.headline: Trump confirms calling Netanyahu crazy in phone conversation
cards.teaser: President Trump acknowledged he used the word crazy to describe Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a phone call.
cards.body:
President Trump confirmed he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu crazy during a phone conversation. Netanyahu downplayed the clash, saying he and Trump have tactical disagreements but agree on broader issues related to Iran.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed hope that ongoing talks between Lebanon and Israel will end hostilities in the region. The exchange between Trump and Netanyahu comes amid questions about U.S. policy toward operations against Hezbollah. Netanyahu characterized the disagreement as tactical rather than strategic.

cards.headline: Federal workers report trauma symptoms after firings deemed unlawful
cards.teaser: Federal employees are experiencing symptoms similar to PTSD after being fired by the Trump administration in actions later ruled unlawful.
cards.body:
Federal workers fired by the Trump administration are experiencing significant mental health effects from their terminations, according to a survey of over 300 dismissed probationary employees. The study found that 95% of respondents reported ongoing mental health impacts, with nearly half experiencing PTSD-like symptoms. About a quarter of those surveyed said they have started new medications to manage their symptoms.

The firings were later determined to be unlawful through legal proceedings. The survey was conducted by 27UNIHTED, a network of former National Institute of Health employees affected by the layoffs.

cards.headline: FBI kills hostage-taker at California bank, releases all captives unharmed
cards.teaser: The FBI shot and killed a man who took multiple people hostage at a California bank, freeing all hostages without injury.
cards.body: Two hostages were freed on Tuesday. The remaining hostages were released on Wednesday after the FBI's intervention ended the standoff.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advances to November runoff
cards.teaser: Mayor Karen Bass secured a spot in the November general election as Spencer Pratt and Nithya Raman compete for the second runoff position.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass won Tuesday's primary election but failed to secure a majority of votes, forcing her into a November runoff. She will face either Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or city council member Nithya Raman in the general election.

As of Wednesday morning with more than 60% of votes counted, Pratt led the race for the second spot with 30% of the vote, while Raman had won 22%. The final tally will determine which candidate will challenge Bass in November.

cards.headline: House Democrats retain seats in California congressional primaries
cards.teaser: Veteran House Democrats defended their positions in California primary elections as redrawn districts faced their first electoral test.
cards.body:
House Democrats held onto seats in California congressional races following primary elections. The contests marked the first test of California's redrawn U.S. House map, which Democrats hope will counter Republican redistricting efforts.

Several key California congressional races now advance to November, with results still pending in some districts. The outcomes will help determine control of the House. California's congressional delegation plays an important role in the balance of power in Washington.

hero.headline: Google increases stock sale to $85 billion to fund AI expansion
hero.body:
Alphabet, Google's parent company, has increased its planned equity raise to $85 billion, making it the largest stock offering in corporate history. The company is pursuing this massive capital raise to finance its artificial intelligence infrastructure investments and address surging demand for its AI services.

The original plan called for an $80 billion raise, which already dwarfed the world's three largest initial public offerings combined. Saudi Aramco raised $25.6 billion in 2019, Alibaba brought in $21.8 billion in 2014, and SoftBank collected $21.3 billion in 2018. The increase to $85 billion underscores Alphabet's commitment to scaling its AI operations as competitors race to develop advanced technology.

The fundraising includes a $10 billion investment from Berkshire Hathaway, the investment group led until recently by Warren Buffett. The deal also consists of a $30 billion initial raise and a $40 billion flexible mechanism that can be deployed gradually over time. Half of the $80 billion is designated for scaling AI infrastructure and global computing capacity, while $40 billion will cover administrative changes related to employee equity award tax obligations.

Alphabet stated that it is experiencing unprecedented demand for its AI solutions and services from both enterprises and consumers, with customer demand exceeding available supply. The company plans to expand its foundational infrastructure to support the significant growth opportunity ahead.

The massive fundraising reflects the capital-intensive nature of the modern AI sector. Alphabet previously indicated that capital expenditure would reach between $180 billion and $190 billion this year, with another significant increase expected in 2027. According to Matt Britzman, a senior equity analyst at Hargreaves Lansdown, the fundraising represents "a clear sign that the AI arms race is moving into a more capital-hungry phase." He added that "long gone are the days when the tech giants were capital-light free cashflow machines."

The stock sale also raises questions about the economics of the AI boom. Despite massive investment in AI infrastructure across the technology industry, meaningful returns to investors have so far been limited. Jim Reid, a market strategist at Deutsche Bank, noted that Alphabet's fundraising reminds investors of the "unprecedented scale of the AI spending boom."

Alphabet shares fell as much as 4.4% following the announcement, and the broader Nasdaq index declined nearly 0.5%. The company is tapping investors for capital before some of its major AI rivals pursue public listings. Anthropic, which developed the Claude chatbot, has filed confidentially for an IPO and is now valued at $965 billion. OpenAI and Elon Musk's xAI are also scheduled to go public this year.

cards.headline: Stock markets fall as oil prices and bond yields rise
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 400 points as investors sold technology stocks and monitored rising energy costs.
cards.body:
Major US stock indexes declined, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling over 425 points. The S&P 500's nine-day winning streak faced pressure as technology stocks sold off and the Nasdaq also traded lower. The retreat from recent record highs came as multiple factors weighed on investor sentiment.

Oil prices ticked higher amid ongoing fighting in the Middle East and uncertainty around US-Iran relations. Bond yields also crept upward during the trading session. The combination of rising yields and energy costs contributed to the pullback in equities, with Alphabet shares among those dragging on the broader market.

cards.headline: Trump administration adopts forced labor rationale for tariffs
cards.teaser: The administration has shifted its legal justification for import duties, citing forced labor concerns as the basis for trade restrictions.
cards.body:
After the Supreme Court struck down many of President Trump's tariffs in February, the administration shifted to a new legal justification focused on forced labor concerns. Officials view this approach as more legally sustainable for imposing trade restrictions going forward.

Critics contend the forced labor rationale masks protectionist aims rather than reflecting genuine concern for labor rights. The administration has begun announcing tariffs under this new framework as it attempts to establish a more durable legal foundation for its trade policy.

cards.headline: US crude oil inventories drop for sixth consecutive week
cards.teaser: American crude stockpiles continued falling as strong export demand and refinery activity drew down supplies.
cards.body:
US crude oil stockpiles fell for the sixth consecutive week, according to the Energy Information Administration. Refineries increased their processing rates and export demand stayed strong, putting downward pressure on domestic reserves.

Gasoline inventories are also declining rapidly. The drop in both crude and gasoline supplies has pushed energy prices higher, with potential effects on consumer costs and inflation.

cards.headline: Administration resists court order on tariff refunds
cards.teaser: The Trump administration has begun repaying some tariff revenue but indicated it may limit how much certain businesses can claim.
cards.body:
The administration started processing refunds for some tariff payments following a court order, but officials signaled they may impose restrictions on the full amounts businesses can recover. The refunds stem from tariffs that courts determined were improperly imposed, creating obligations for the government to return collected revenue.

The administration's approach suggests an effort to limit the financial impact of the court ruling while technically complying with the order. Businesses that paid the disputed tariffs are seeking full reimbursement, but the government's signals about potential limitations have created uncertainty about how much money companies will ultimately receive.

cards.headline: Home sellers withdraw listings at fastest pace since 2020
cards.teaser: Homeowners are pulling properties off the market at near-record rates as buyers resist paying asking prices.
cards.body:
Sellers removed homes from the market at the fastest pace since 2020, according to a study from Redfin. The surge in withdrawn listings reflects a standoff between sellers expecting higher prices and buyers who are holding firm on what they are willing to pay. The dynamic has created a stalemate in many housing markets across the country.

The trend helps explain why some homes sit on the market significantly longer than others. Properties that remain listed often face price reductions or represent sellers with greater urgency to complete a sale. The high rate of withdrawn listings suggests many homeowners would rather wait than accept current market conditions.

cards.headline: CBS News editor addresses Scott Pelley firing
cards.teaser: Bari Weiss said in her first public comments that the longtime correspondent broke trust within the newsroom.
cards.body:
Bari Weiss, CBS News editor in chief, publicly commented for the first time on Scott Pelley's firing from 60 Minutes, saying the veteran correspondent had "broken" trust in the newsroom and that his departure was a path he chose.

The firing followed a confrontation at a staff meeting where Pelley accused leadership of "murdering" the news show. In a statement, Pelley claimed CBS executives instructed him to inject falsehoods and bias into reporting and to allow politicians input on interviews. He defended 60 Minutes' decades-long success on journalistic integrity and quality.

hero.headline: Instagram notifies users targeted in AI chatbot hack attacks
hero.body:
Instagram has begun alerting users whose accounts were targeted by hackers who exploited the platform's AI-powered support chatbot. The notifications come after attackers found ways to take over accounts even following Meta's announced fix to the chatbot vulnerability.

The breach involved hackers manipulating Meta's AI support system to gain unauthorized access to user accounts. Meta had previously stated it resolved the security flaw in its AI chatbot, but victims continued to report compromised accounts after the supposed fix. The company is now reaching out directly to affected users to inform them their accounts were targeted in these attacks.

The incident highlights ongoing security challenges as companies integrate AI systems into customer service tools. Meta's AI chatbot was designed to help users with account issues, but attackers discovered methods to abuse the system for account takeovers. The exact mechanism hackers used to bypass the chatbot's security remains unclear, though the continued attacks after Meta's initial fix suggest the vulnerability proved more complex than initially assessed.

Meta has not disclosed how many users received notifications about the targeting, nor has the company provided specifics about what additional security measures have been implemented beyond the earlier fix. The notifications represent an effort to inform users who may need to take additional steps to secure their accounts, such as changing passwords or reviewing recent account activity.

The chatbot attacks add to a series of security incidents affecting Meta's platforms. As social media companies increasingly deploy AI tools to handle user interactions at scale, the systems present new attack surfaces for malicious actors. The Instagram notifications signal Meta's acknowledgment that the threat extended beyond its initial mitigation efforts, though the company has not commented on whether the vulnerability has now been fully resolved or if additional security work continues.

cards.headline: Ultrahuman reports data breach from malware on employee laptop
cards.teaser: The wearable ring maker says customer wellness data was accessed through an internal tool after hackers obtained credentials from an infected employee device.
cards.body:
Ultrahuman, a maker of health-tracking wearable rings, disclosed a data breach affecting its customers. Attackers gained access to wellness data through an internal company tool after stealing credentials from an employee's laptop that had been infected with malware.

The breach exposed customer information stored within Ultrahuman's systems, though specifics about the scope and types of data compromised remain limited based on the company's public statements.

cards.headline: Apple doubles MacBook Neo production amid strong demand
cards.teaser: The company increased manufacturing of its latest laptop model as sales outpace other MacBook lines in a declining PC market.
cards.body:
Apple has doubled production of its MacBook Neo following higher than expected consumer demand. The laptop has become the company's best-selling MacBook model, outperforming both the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro lines.

The MacBook Neo represents a bright spot in an otherwise declining global PC market. Industry analysts note the device is attracting a new generation of buyers to Apple's laptop lineup, driving the company's decision to ramp up manufacturing to meet ongoing demand.

cards.headline: AI music startup Suno raises $400 million despite copyright lawsuits
cards.teaser: The company is now valued at over $5.4 billion, more than doubling its valuation from seven months ago.
cards.body:
Suno, an AI music generation startup, has raised $400 million in new funding despite facing ongoing copyright lawsuits. The investment values the company at over $5.4 billion, marking a significant jump from its $2.45 billion valuation seven months earlier.

The funding round demonstrates investor confidence in AI music generation technology even as the company navigates copyright litigation related to its systems. The legal challenges have not prevented backing from flowing into the startup's continued growth.

cards.headline: Google releases Fitbit Air blueprints for custom accessories
cards.teaser: The company published CAD drawings and specifications allowing anyone to design and manufacture bands and other add-ons for the wearable device.
cards.body:
Google has released CAD drawings and technical specifications for its Fitbit Air wearable, enabling third-party manufacturers and hobbyists to create custom accessories. The blueprints include detailed measurements and guidelines for making compatible bands and other attachments.

The move opens the door for 3D-printed accessories and alternative band designs beyond what Google offers directly. The company's specifications welcome bicep bands and other mounting options, expanding how users can wear the fitness tracking device beyond traditional wrist placement.

cards.headline: Carvana partners with Bezos-backed Slate Auto for new car sales
cards.teaser: The used car retailer received a warrant to buy shares in Slate last year, with both companies backed by Guggenheim Partners CEO Mark Walter.
cards.body:
Carvana is partnering with Slate Auto to expand into new vehicle sales. According to documents obtained by TechCrunch, Carvana received a warrant last year to purchase shares in Slate, positioning it to enter the new car market through this relationship.

Slate Auto has backing from Jeff Bezos, and Mark Walter, CEO of Guggenheim Partners, holds significant investments in both Carvana and Slate.

cards.headline: Amazon to display AI-generated product images in search results
cards.teaser: The retailer will use visual search and AI to create images matching search queries, saying the feature will guide users to products.
cards.body:
Amazon is rolling out AI-generated product images in search results. The retailer uses visual search and artificial intelligence to create images that match customer search queries, aiming to guide users toward relevant products in its catalog.

The move represents Amazon's effort to enhance the search experience by leveraging synthetic imagery alongside its product catalog.

hero.headline: Browns receive first-round pick from Rams for Myles Garrett trade to AFC North
hero.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks. The deal sends one of the NFL's premier defensive players to Los Angeles as the franchise seeks to strengthen its championship contention.

Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since the Browns selected him with the first overall pick in 2017, he has established himself among the league's elite defensive talents. He holds the record for most sacks with 125.5, most pressures with 413, and most tackles for loss with 149 of any player since his draft year. In 2025, he set a single-season sacks record with 23 despite playing for a struggling team.

Garrett had requested a trade from Cleveland in 2024 after the Browns finished with a 3-14 record. He expressed his desire to play for a team with genuine championship prospects. Despite his trade request, the Browns signed him to a four-year, $160 million extension that made him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time. The deal included an average annual salary of $40 million and $122.8 million in guaranteed money.

The 2025 season proved difficult for Cleveland, which finished 5-12 and missed the playoffs for the second consecutive year. Garrett remained the franchise's standout performer, earning All-Pro recognition. The team also made coaching changes, firing Kevin Stefanski and hiring former Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken in January.

General manager Andrew Berry facilitated the trade after Garrett and the Browns agreed to restructure his contract in March. The modification deferred option payments across the 2026-28 seasons, allowing the organization to complete the deal.

"As discussions intensified we were stuck at a legitimate crossroads: do we hold on to a truly generational player who has become the identity of our team, or do we make the difficult decision that we think is best for the organization over the long run?" Berry said after announcing the trade.

Cleveland received a 2027 first-round selection, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round selection alongside Verse. The 25-year-old linebacker was selected by the Rams in the first round of the 2024 draft and earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. He recorded 12 career sacks and 22 tackles for loss.

The Rams, who lost to the eventual champion Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC Championship Game, are pursuing another Super Bowl appearance. This trade reunites Garrett with quarterback Matthew Stafford, last season's Associated Press NFL MVP and Defensive Player of the Year, marking their first time as teammates.

cards.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo trade speculation centers on Heat as NBA Finals begin
cards.teaser: Reports indicate the Miami Heat lead the pursuit of Milwaukee Bucks star Giannis Antetokounmpo as trade speculation intensifies.
cards.body:
The Miami Heat emerged as the apparent frontrunner to acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo from the Milwaukee Bucks as the NBA Finals tipped off. Multiple reports linked several teams to the two-time MVP, with Miami drawing the most attention as a potential landing spot.

The Portland Trail Blazers and Boston Celtics also surfaced in trade speculation surrounding Antetokounmpo. The timing of the reports coincides with the start of the Finals, traditionally a period when front offices evaluate roster changes for the upcoming season. Antetokounmpo has spent his entire NBA career with Milwaukee since entering the league in 2013.

cards.headline: World number one Aryna Sabalenka loses French Open quarterfinal to Diana Shnaider
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka fell to Diana Shnaider 3-6, 7-5, 6-0 in a French Open quarterfinal upset.
cards.body:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka crashed out of the French Open in the quarterfinals, losing to 25th seed Diana Shnaider 3-6, 7-5, 6-0. After winning the opening set, Sabalenka's performance deteriorated dramatically, losing 10 consecutive games and failing to win a single game in the final set.

In her post-match press conference, Sabalenka expressed her distress, stating she wanted to "quit tennis right now" before acknowledging she would reassess her mental state in the coming days. The defeat represents a significant meltdown for the top seed, who had entered as the tournament favorite.

cards.headline: Qualifier Maja Chwalinska reaches French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: Maja Chwalinska defeated Anna Kalinskaya to reach her first Grand Slam semifinal at the French Open.
cards.body:
Qualifier Maja Chwalinska continued her impressive French Open run by defeating Anna Kalinskaya in the quarterfinals. The victory marks her first Grand Slam semifinal appearance, representing a breakthrough achievement at the major tournament level.

Chwalinska's progression from the qualifying rounds to the semifinals demonstrates an exceptional performance at Roland Garros. Her advancement comes amid several surprising results at this year's tournament, including world number one Aryna Sabalenka's shock exit from the competition.

cards.headline: SEC and Big Ten criticize proposed Protect College Sports Act
cards.teaser: The two major conferences issued a joint statement identifying problems with legislation aimed at regulating conference expansion.
cards.body:
The Southeastern Conference and Big Ten released a joint statement opposing aspects of the proposed Protect College Sports Act ahead of a Senate hearing. The conferences cited critical issues with the bill, which addresses college sports governance and conference realignment. The White House is reviewing the legislation.

The bill comes amid ongoing expansion by major conferences that has reshaped college athletics. Former Alabama coach Nick Saban testified before Congress on college sports matters. The legislation attempts to impose federal oversight on conference membership changes and other structural decisions in college athletics.

cards.headline: Andoni Iraola set to be named Liverpool head coach
cards.teaser: Liverpool is expected to announce Andoni Iraola as its new head coach this week.
cards.body:
Andoni Iraola has agreed a deal in principle to become Liverpool's new head coach on a two-year contract. The Spaniard replaces Arne Slot, who was sacked on Saturday. Negotiations between Iraola and Liverpool's sporting director Richard Hughes progressed quickly, with an official announcement expected this week.

Iraola's assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper will join him at Anfield as part of the backroom team setup.

cards.headline: Rory McIlroy says he will continue selective PGA Tour schedule
cards.teaser: The golfer said he plans to pick and choose which events he plays under the tour's new schedule format.
cards.body:
Rory McIlroy will continue his selective approach to PGA Tour events under the new schedule structure. The golfer said he will "pick and choose" which tournaments to enter because it allows him to maintain balance in his life.

McIlroy's strategy reflects a broader shift among players adjusting to the PGA Tour's revised schedule. His willingness to play as a part-timer demonstrates how the tour's changes have given competitors greater flexibility in managing their competitive calendars alongside other commitments.

hero.headline: CBS Fires Scott Pelley From 60 Minutes After Management Clash
hero.body:
CBS News has terminated Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at 60 Minutes, following a heated confrontation with the network's new leadership. The firing marks a dramatic escalation in management changes at the long-running news program.

The conflict centered on sweeping staff cuts announced the previous week. On Thursday, CBS News management terminated the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi, without publicly explaining the reasons. During a heated staff meeting Monday morning with newly appointed executive editor Nick Bilton and other executives, Pelley directly attacked Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief who joined in October.

"She's murdering 60 Minutes," Pelley said at the meeting. "She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that."

CBS executives attempted to meet with Pelley after the initial terminations, but he did not engage. By Tuesday, Pelley met with Weiss and other executives, who conveyed that his conduct was inappropriate. That evening, Bilton sent Pelley a message terminating him for cause, citing his behavior in the meeting.

"Yesterday, you hijacked my first meeting with staff to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt," Bilton wrote.

Pelley subsequently issued a public statement accusing CBS News executives of silencing employees and instructing him "to inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He wrote that 60 Minutes has been the top program in America because audiences "find integrity, quality, and humanity in our stories."

Pelley's departure creates significant uncertainty for the program. With journalist Anderson Cooper announcing earlier this year that he would leave the show, 60 Minutes now has only three full-time correspondents heading into its 59th season: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and L Jon Wertheim. Norah O'Donnell contributes occasionally.

The timing compounds existing tensions at the network. Days before his firing, Pelley publicly praised Alfonsi at the News and Documentary Emmy Awards, hours after she announced her contract would not be renewed. He also praised an 18-year-old scholarship recipient who said the current leadership "stains the legacy of Mike Wallace," the legendary 60 Minutes correspondent.

Pelley joined CBS News in 1989 and anchored the CBS Evening News from 2011 to 2017 before focusing on 60 Minutes reporting. His career included work as chief White House correspondent and international reporting assignments.

The dismissal highlights broader tensions about editorial direction and management philosophy under Weiss, whose appointment has proven controversial within CBS News ranks. As the network rebuilds its correspondent roster, industry observers are watching to see whether other veteran journalists will remain with the program.

cards.headline: Disney Adjusts Super Bowl Ad Sales After Advertiser Pushback on Pricing
cards.teaser: Disney has begun moving Super Bowl commercial time after advertisers balked at the network's pricing demands for its 2027 broadcast.
cards.body:
Disney has started relocating Super Bowl commercial inventory following resistance from advertisers over the company's pricing strategy. The network had pressed sponsors to pay $10 million for a 30-second spot, while also requesting an additional $10 million match for other inventory tied to its broadcast of Super Bowl LXI in 2027.

After what sources described as significant complaints from the advertising community, Disney sold a portion of the commercial time. The negotiations highlight the tension between networks seeking premium prices for marquee sports events and advertisers operating under tightened budgets.

cards.headline: Sara Bareilles Announces New Album and Tour After Seven-Year Recording Gap
cards.teaser: The singer will release Good Grief on Aug. 28, followed by a North American theater tour in September and October.
cards.body:
Sara Bareilles is releasing her first studio album in seven years, titled Good Grief, on August 28. The album marks the singer-songwriter's return to recording after maintaining a low public profile since before the pandemic.

Following the album release, Bareilles will embark on a North American theater tour in September and October, signaling her full re-emergence as a recording and performing artist.

cards.headline: TV Networks Push Sports Programming as Advertisers Reduce Upfront Spending
cards.teaser: Major broadcasters are shifting focus to sports content as Madison Avenue cuts traditional programming budgets.
cards.body:
Television networks and streaming services are aggressively pitching sports programming to advertisers as Madison Avenue cuts back on traditional upfront commitments. The industry is reducing budgets historically allocated to dramas, comedies and reality shows.

Networks are betting that live sports content can command premium advertising rates despite contracting overall ad spending. The strategy reflects a shift toward programming that attracts live audiences and counters the industry's broader move toward on-demand viewing.

cards.headline: Weezer Releases New Single Ahead of August Album
cards.teaser: The band previewed its upcoming self-titled album with the track We Might As Well Be Strangers featuring Wednesday.
cards.body:
Weezer has released a new single, "We Might As Well Be Strangers," featuring the artist Wednesday. The track serves as a preview of the band's upcoming self-titled album arriving August 21.

The album includes the previously released single "Shine Again." This continues Weezer's tradition of self-titled albums throughout their career.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Explains Turning Down Saturday Night Live Over Dyslexia Concerns
cards.teaser: The actor said he declined to host the show because of anxiety about reading changing cue cards.
cards.body:
Tom Holland turned down an offer to host Saturday Night Live due to concerns about his dyslexia. The actor cited anxiety about reading cue cards that change during the live broadcast as a key factor in his decision to decline the opportunity.

Holland has been widely praised for publicly discussing his dyslexia and how it influences his professional decisions. His candid approach to the condition has resonated with supporters who view his openness as a powerful message.

cards.headline: Dropout CEO Sam Reich Discusses Emmy Prospects and Streaming Strategy
cards.teaser: The comedy streamer held its first FYC event at the Laugh Factory as it seeks industry recognition.
cards.body:
Sam Reich, CEO of independent comedy streamer Dropout, held the company's first awards consideration event at the Laugh Factory. Rather than chasing a specific outcome, Reich framed the gathering as an opportunity to establish Dropout's presence within the entertainment industry and participate in the awards conversation.

Reich noted unexpected fan interest from personalities like Abby Lee Miller and discussed the platform's upcoming projects, including an animated adaptation of the fantasy series Dimension 20. Game Changer, one of Dropout's flagship shows, was among the titles featured at the event.

hero.headline: Senate Republicans remove $1 billion White House ballroom funding from budget bill
hero.body:
Senate Republicans have stripped language from a revised budget reconciliation bill that would have allocated up to $1 billion for security upgrades to a proposed White House ballroom. The decision was made internally before the Memorial Day recess, with the change becoming public when the revised package was released Wednesday.

The ballroom project, championed by President Trump, would have created a 90,000-square-foot facility on White House grounds. The removal marks a significant setback for the initiative after the funding had been included in earlier versions of the reconciliation package that Republicans are using to advance budget priorities without Democratic support.

Budget reconciliation allows the majority party to pass fiscal legislation with a simple majority in the Senate, bypassing the standard 60-vote threshold required to overcome a filibuster. This procedural tool enables Republicans to advance their budget agenda without needing Democratic votes.

The decision to remove the ballroom provision came after internal discussions among Senate Republicans, who control the chamber. The revised bill was unveiled Wednesday without the ballroom language, representing a significant change from the earlier draft. Senate Republican leadership did not provide a public explanation for the removal or the timing of the announcement.

The reconciliation package continues progressing through the legislative process without the ballroom funding included. The move reflects internal GOP calculations about what provisions could survive the legislative process and maintain party unity on the broader budget package.

This development comes as Congress navigates significant fiscal and policy disagreements. The Senate has been engaged in disputes with House Republican leadership over government funding, particularly regarding Department of Homeland Security appropriations. House Speaker Mike Johnson has indicated his chamber will pursue alternative funding approaches, setting up potential conflicts between the two chambers over budget priorities.

The broader reconciliation effort remains one of the Republican majority's main vehicles for advancing the Trump administration's policy agenda. With Democrats unable to block reconciliation measures that stay within budgetary parameters, Republicans have been working to include various priorities in these bills.

The White House has not yet commented publicly on the removal of the ballroom provision from the reconciliation bill. It remains unclear whether the administration will pursue alternative funding mechanisms for the proposed facility or whether the project will be shelved entirely.

The decision by Senate Republicans to strip the funding suggests concern among some members about the optics of allocating such substantial resources to the project during a period of significant government funding debates and fiscal pressures. The removal allows Republicans to focus the reconciliation bill on other priorities while potentially addressing concerns from members who questioned the appropriateness of the ballroom expenditure.

cards.headline: Trump nominates housing official Bill Pulte as director of national intelligence
cards.teaser: Senator Mitch McConnell issued a warning about qualifications needed for the intelligence post after the nomination was announced.
cards.body:
President Trump has nominated Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as director of national intelligence. The role requires overseeing 18 intelligence agencies and serving as the president's principal intelligence adviser.

Senator Mitch McConnell issued a statement Wednesday cautioning that anyone appointed to the position must possess "extensive national security experience." Senator Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, has also raised concerns about Pulte's appointment.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as an official in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico on Tuesday. If successful in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

The primary victory sets up a general election contest in November for the governorship. Haaland previously served in federal office before her role in the Biden administration, representing New Mexico in Congress.

cards.headline: Republican James Gallagher wins California House special election
cards.teaser: The state assemblymember will fill the seat left vacant after Representative Doug LaMalfa died in January.
cards.body:
California State Assemblymember James Gallagher won a special election Tuesday to represent California's 1st Congressional District in the House. Gallagher, who received President Trump's endorsement, will fill the seat left vacant after Representative Doug LaMalfa died in January.

The victory gives a slight boost to the Republican majority in the House. Gallagher will serve the remainder of the term representing the northern California district.

cards.headline: Homeland Security secretary reviewing contracts signed under predecessor
cards.teaser: Markwayne Mullin told lawmakers he is examining agreements pursued by Kristi Noem that may have involved her allies.
cards.body:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told House lawmakers he is reviewing contracts his predecessor Kristi Noem pursued that may have connections to her allies. He committed to providing Congress with a complete list of cancelled contracts.

The disclosure came during questioning from Representative Bennie Thompson, the committee's top Democrat. Mullin did not identify which specific contracts were under review or describe the nature of the alleged ties to Noem's associates.

cards.headline: House lawmakers aim to release draft artificial intelligence bill by end of week
cards.teaser: Representative Jay Obernolte said negotiators are finalizing details of the bipartisan legislation.
cards.body:
House negotiators working on bipartisan artificial intelligence legislation are targeting the end of the week to unveil a draft bill, according to Representative Jay Obernolte. The lawmakers are currently resolving remaining technical details in the proposal.

The legislation represents a congressional effort to establish federal guidelines for the rapidly developing artificial intelligence field. The draft bill would mark a significant milestone in bipartisan regulatory efforts in this space.

cards.headline: California governor primary results remain too close to call
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra compete against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton to replace Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
The primary race to replace California Governor Gavin Newsom remained too close to call Wednesday, with early results showing a tight contest among multiple candidates. Republican Steve Hilton led the field with 28%, followed closely by Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer.

California's top-two primary system advances the two candidates with the most votes regardless of party affiliation to the general election in November. With many ballots still being counted, final results were expected to take several days to determine.
